review: Targeted primary-source review; not a systematic review or exhaustive all-specialty content curation
retrieval_limits: Consensus deep synthesis was not dispatched because of credit limits; one paper search returned candidates. Firecrawl retrieved official guidance and several primary abstracts then hit rate/credit limits. Per user instruction no further Consensus or Firecrawl calls were made; remaining selected checks used direct primary-source access. Unread full tables/protocols/device manuals are not claimed as curated.

sources.title: ESICM circulatory shock and hemodynamic monitoring guideline, 2025
sources.implication_and_limits: Adult critically ill; primary abstract and official society material checked. Dynamic assessment when applicable, multimodal perfusion, echo and escalation of monitoring. Full 50-statement table not imported; graded statements differ from good-practice statements.

sources.title: Surviving Sepsis Campaign adult guideline, 2026
sources.implication_and_limits: Official recommendations published 23 March 2026 checked. Initial MAP 65; a conditional 60–65 range for age65+; conditional initial crystalloid guidance with individualization; peripheral pressor evidence has unspecified universal limits. Local adoption required.

sources.title: ANDROMEDA-SHOCK, 2019
sources.implication_and_limits: Primary abstract checked. CRT-targeted versus lactate-targeted septic shock protocol did not meet its primary 28-day mortality comparison. Adjunctive CRT does not become a single-marker treatment command.

sources.title: ANDROMEDA-SHOCK-2, 2025
sources.implication_and_limits: Primary abstract checked. Early septic shock personalized CRT/phenotype protocol improved a hierarchical composite, mainly via duration of vital support. Do not describe this as proven isolated mortality benefit or copy trial protocol into an unvalidated bedside algorithm.

sources.title: FRESH fluid response evaluation trial, 2020
sources.implication_and_limits: Primary abstract checked. Flow-based PLR-guided strategy had lower fluid balance in a relatively small trial. Method/platform/protocol and study limitations preclude universal outcome or every-device claims.

sources.title: CLOVERS, 2023
sources.implication_and_limits: Primary abstract checked. Early sepsis-induced hypotension after initial fluids: restrictive/early-pressor versus liberal strategy did not significantly change the primary mortality endpoint. Not evidence that fluids or pressors are never indicated.

sources.title: CLASSIC, 2022
sources.implication_and_limits: Primary abstract checked. ICU septic shock after initial fluid: restricted versus standard strategy had similar 90-day mortality. Phase and rescue conditions matter.

sources.title: ARISE FLUIDS, 2026
sources.implication_and_limits: Primary abstract checked directly after connector limits. Published online 11 June 2026, after SSC2026 publication. Early ED septic shock: restrictive/early-pressor strategy did not improve days alive out of hospital at90days; pulmonary-edema findings do not establish universal superiority.

sources.title: SOAP II, 2010
sources.implication_and_limits: Primary abstract checked. Dopamine versus norepinephrine in shock: more arrhythmic events with dopamine; overall primary mortality not significantly different. Cardiogenic subgroup results are not a universal all-agent comparison.

sources.title: DOREMI, 2021
sources.implication_and_limits: Primary abstract checked. Small cardiogenic shock trial found no significant primary composite difference between milrinone and dobutamine. Not equivalence proof for all patients or a dosing protocol.

sources.title: ACC concise cardiogenic shock clinical guidance, 2025
sources.implication_and_limits: Primary citation and official ACC guidance announcement checked. Early recognition, cause/perfusion/congestion assessment, team pathways and invasive hemodynamic profiling. This is expert guidance; not proof PAC insertion itself improves survival in every patient.

sources.title: SCAI shock-stage consensus update, 2022
sources.implication_and_limits: Official society summary checked. Stage, etiology/phenotype and other risk modifiers are distinct; arrest modifiers and trajectories matter. Exact table requires local versioned curation before automated candidate staging.

sources.title: ECLS-SHOCK, 2023
sources.implication_and_limits: Primary abstract checked. Early ECLS in infarct-related cardiogenic shock with planned revascularization did not reduce30-day mortality and increased bleeding/vascular complications. Not evidence against every carefully selected rescue use.

sources.title: DanGer-Shock, 2024
sources.implication_and_limits: Primary publication checked directly. Selected STEMI cardiogenic-shock population: microaxial pump reduced180-day mortality with greater adverse events. Strict eligibility, device/center expertise and competing harms prevent all-shock extrapolation.

sources.title: SMART, 2018
sources.implication_and_limits: Primary abstract checked. Pragmatic cluster-crossover ICU trial favored balanced fluid for a kidney/death composite. Composite, design, population and later trials limit universal mortality claims.

sources.title: PLUS, 2022
sources.implication_and_limits: Primary abstract checked directly. ICU balanced multielectrolyte solution versus saline did not reduce primary mortality or AKI outcomes. Product and population specificity remain relevant.

sources.title: BaSICS, 2021
sources.implication_and_limits: Primary abstract checked. Balanced solution versus saline did not significantly reduce90-day mortality. Do not imply every balanced-fluid product has identical benefit in every context.

sources.title: SEPSISPAM, 2014
sources.implication_and_limits: Primary abstract checked directly. Higher versus lower MAP in septic shock did not improve mortality; higher target had more new AF. Chronic-hypertension subgroup kidney findings require contextual interpretation.

sources.title: 65 trial, 2020
sources.implication_and_limits: Primary abstract checked. Adults65+ with vasodilatory hypotension: reduced pressor exposure/permissive hypotension did not significantly reduce the unadjusted primary mortality outcome. Not a universal low-pressure strategy.
